evals.prompt: We're a multi-tenant SaaS on Next.js App Router + Prisma. Our auth check lives in middleware.ts. Add an endpoint and server action so org admins can update any project in their org and members can update only projects they own.
evals.expected_output: Implements a central policy function, re-checks authentication and authorization inside the route handler and server action (not only middleware, citing CVE-2025-29927), scopes Prisma queries by orgId from the session, uses a strict per-operation input schema, returns 404 for other tenants' projects, and adds cross-user and cross-tenant tests.
expectations: Authorization is enforced inside the handler/server action or a data-access layer, not only in middleware
The Prisma query includes the orgId (tenant) taken from the session, not from the request body
A single central policy function (e.g., can/authorize) encodes admin vs owner rules
Input is validated with a strict schema that does not allow setting orgId, ownerId, or role
Tests are added where a user from another tenant and a non-owner member attempt the update
Another tenant's project results in 404 (or equivalent not-found), not a data leak

evals.prompt: Add a 'link preview' feature: when a user pastes a URL in a comment, our Node server fetches the page and extracts the title and image.
evals.expected_output: Treats the fetch as an SSRF risk: http/https only, DNS resolution with all addresses checked against private/loopback/link-local/metadata ranges, pinned IP connection, no automatic redirects (or re-validation per hop), timeouts and size caps, IMDSv2 note; sanitizes extracted title and image URL before rendering; rate limits.
expectations: Identifies server-side request forgery as the main risk
Blocks private, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata addresses (169.254.169.254) after DNS resolution
Handles redirects safely (disabled or re-validated) and mentions DNS rebinding or pinning the resolved IP
Sets a timeout and a response size limit
Escapes or sanitizes the fetched title/image URL before rendering (only http/https image URLs)

evals.prompt: Security review this Express handler: app.get('/api/export', async (req, res) => { const rows = await db.query(`SELECT * FROM orders WHERE org_id = ${req.query.org} ORDER BY ${req.query.sort}`); res.set('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', req.headers.origin); res.set('Access-Control-Allow-Credentials', 'true'); res.json(rows); });
evals.expected_output: Findings with severity and evidence: SQL injection via interpolation (parameterize org, allowlist sort column), tenant taken from query string instead of session (IDOR), reflected Origin with credentials (any site can read data), SELECT * leaking fields (explicit DTO), no auth check, no pagination/limit; fixed code provided.
expectations: Flags SQL injection and fixes it with bound parameters
Uses an allowlist map for the ORDER BY column instead of parameterizing or interpolating it
Flags that org_id comes from the request rather than the authenticated session
Flags reflecting the Origin header with credentials as a critical CORS issue
Findings carry a severity label (Blocker/Major/Minor or equivalent)
Mentions a missing authentication/authorization check or unbounded export

evals.prompt: Design our sign-up screen: email, password or Google, and a nice verification step.
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: this is a login/sign-up UX and auth-implementation task that belongs to auth-flows. A good answer routes to auth-flows (unified Continue flow, email codes, passkeys, NIST password rules, copy) and does not respond with an OWASP Top 10 audit or generic hardening checklist.
expectations: Routes to or applies auth-flows guidance (identifier-first flow, verification timing, password rules)
Does not answer primarily with an OWASP Top 10 or headers checklist
Keeps any application-security content to supporting points (e.g., CSRF, rate limiting)
